description: First-pass triage of a domain flagged by detection tooling, a user report, or upstream feed. Capture the registration footprint, current DNS resolution, and any URLs observed underneath, so a reviewer can decide whether it warrants escalation.
name: Suspicious domain triage

structure.help: The domain itself plus context for why it's being looked at.
structure.label: Overview

structure.help: The bare domain (no scheme, no path). Use the punycode form for IDN — capture the visible Unicode form in the *Why suspicious* field below.
structure.label: Domain

structure.help: When you first encountered this domain. ISO 8601.
structure.label: Date observed

structure.help: Where this domain came to your attention — e.g. *DNS sinkhole alert*, *user report*, *URLhaus feed*, *brand-monitoring vendor X*.
structure.label: Report source

structure.help: Free-form Markdown — what makes the domain suspicious. Lookalike of a brand domain? Newly-registered? Hosting a phishing kit? Visible Unicode form (for IDNs)? Saved as an EventReport attached to the new event.
structure.label: Why suspicious

structure.help: What the domain currently resolves to. Capture a snapshot — fast-flux operators may rotate the answer minute by minute.
structure.label: DNS resolution

structure.help: Single domain-ip object grouping the domain with its observed resolution(s). Use the **+ Add another instance** below if the domain resolves to several distinct IPs.
structure.label: Domain → IP resolution

relations.help_override: Same value as the *Domain* field above.
What the domain resolved to at *first-seen* time.
Earliest known time of this domain → ip pair.
Most recent observation of this pair.

structure.help: WHOIS data. Recently-registered domains and bulk-registered batches are strong triage signals.
structure.label: Registration footprint

structure.help: Standard WHOIS fields. Most analysts only fill creation-date, registrar, and registrant-email at first triage; the full record can be appended later.
structure.label: WHOIS

relations.help_override: Same value as the *Domain* field above.
Strong triage signal — domains <30 days old are common in phishing infrastructure.
Some registrars are over-represented in abuse reporting.
When unprivacy-shielded, this often correlates with other domains in the same campaign.

structure.help: URLs, paths, or content seen on the domain. Helpful both for evidence and for downstream URL-blocking.
structure.label: Observed under this domain

structure.help: Full URL — captures the path component which is often the giveaway for phishing pages. One URL per entry; defang on copy if your tooling requires.
structure.label: Observed URL

structure.help: If you have the JA3 of the TLS server hello — useful for identifying common phishing-kit hosting infrastructure.
structure.label: TLS JA3 fingerprint

structure.help: TLP, kill-chain phase, and any actor / brand attribution.
structure.label: Classification

structure.help: Pick one. Override the default if the analyst's TLP differs.
structure.label: TLP

structure.help: Most often *delivery* or *command and control* depending on the domain's role.
structure.label: Kill chain phase

structure.help: Optional. Speculation here pollutes correlation — leave blank unless multiple independent indicators support the attribution.
structure.label: Suspected threat actor

structure.content: **A note on freshness:** DNS resolution and TLS fingerprints are point-in-time observations. If the domain is still active when this event is reviewed, re-pull the WHOIS and re-resolve before acting on the IPs — these change fast on adversary infrastructure.
